editorNote: A quiet day for releases: a language update, a Google coding model, and local-inference attempts at both ends of the hardware range, plus one paper on what a chatty model could smuggle out.

stories.headline: Rust 1.100 stabilizes the never type and the Allocator trait
stories.summary: Rust 1.100 makes `!` a stable, nameable type and stabilizes the core Allocator trait so custom allocators work with Vec and Box. Cargo now warns about unused dependencies and stabilizes dependency cooldowns.
stories.whyItMatters: The never-type fallback change in editions before 2024 can break some existing code, so upgrades merit a build check.

stories.headline: Google ships Gemini 4 Hydrogen and an 'Orchestrator' mode in Antigravity
stories.summary: Hydrogen is rolling out to paid Google AI Pro and Ultra users; Orchestrator pairs it with Gemini 4 Carbon, using Carbon for planning and Hydrogen for edits and tests. Google says this gets near-Carbon results on Terminal-Bench 4.1 with about 24% less quota and 19% less time.
stories.whyItMatters: Those are Google's own benchmark claims, and the post lists no per-token prices; access is by subscription tier.

stories.headline: Brave's Search API now takes per-request payments from agents via x402
stories.summary: Agents can pay in USDC on Base for each query, with no account or API key: a request gets an HTTP 402 with the price, then retries with a signed payment. Pricing is $0.005 per request, and Brave covers gas fees for a limited time.
stories.whyItMatters: It is a concrete case of a vendor letting software buyers pay per call without signing up.

sourceLinks.title: Brave Search API now accepts agentic payments

stories.headline: Edge0 releases Edge0-145B, an open on-device mixture-of-experts model
stories.summary: The 145B-parameter model activates about 10B parameters per step and tiers weights across GPU memory, system RAM and SSD, with a reported 29GB peak memory and 80+ tokens/s decode. The benchmark figures are Edge0's own, and a technical report is still to come.
stories.whyItMatters: If the claims hold, a frontier-style model would fit on a high-end laptop; they are unverified.

stories.headline: smolmaxxing pushes LLMs onto TV boxes, a 2013 iPad and a budget phone
stories.summary: The MIT-licensed llama.cpp patch reports an 80B mixture-of-experts model at roughly 3 tokens/s on a phone with ~3GB free, using custom kernels, trimmed vocabulary and paging weights from flash.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows how far memory tricks stretch sparse models on very old hardware, at single-digit speeds.

stories.headline: 'Synthesis Smuggling': an LLM could hide inferences about you in text you share
stories.summary: An arXiv paper describes a threat where a model infers traits such as age group or gender in ordinary conversation and encodes them in harmless-looking output using invisible characters or word choice. The authors demonstrated it with two open-weight models.
stories.whyItMatters: It points to a covert channel through which user-shared model outputs could leak personal inferences; the evidence is a proof of concept.
